Close booktiger's Diary [转载]可不能“随手一标”！ Posted by booktiger on 17 October 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 可不能“随手一标”！ 来源：国家安全部 2026年10月17日07:03 北京 https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Xri2QFc-6VPpZ6QLBaqjgw 一张看似普通的网络地图，一个出于“兴趣”的随手标注，竟可能危害国家秘密安全。近年来，随着地理信息技术的普及，“开放地图”平台逐渐走入公众视野，但其背后隐藏的国家安全风险却不容忽视。 一个“爱好”带来的麻烦 2021年，许某在社交媒体上被一张带有艺术风格的路网地图所吸引。出于好奇，他开始接触境外开放地图平台，并违法“翻墙”访问。许某凭借对居住地周边环境的了解，以及从互联网搜集的公开信息，开始在境外开放地图平台上标注各类地理信息，多次标注军队等涉密敏感单位的位置信息。国家安全机关发现许某违法行为后迅速采取行动，依法对其开展审查。面对审查，许某懊悔道：“我完全没想到，自己只是出于爱好做点标记，竟会触犯法律，威胁国家安全。”国家安全机关向其宣讲了相关法律法规，讲明了其行为的危害性，并依法对其进行处理。许某表示已深刻认识到错误，并积极配合消除隐患。 随手一标，隐患巨大 “开放地图”一般指数据开源、可自由使用与编辑的地图项目，经常由全球志愿者共同创建、编辑并免费共享地理数据，在碳中和、城乡交通建设、灾害风险评估研究等方面具备相应应用价值。但如果在开放地图平台上标注我国涉密敏感地理信息，就有可能被不法分子利用，对我国家安全造成危害。不法分子无需动用复杂的技术手段，仅凭开放地图便能轻易获取我国涉密敏感单位的位置、规模等信息，并据此在军事基地等涉密敏感单位附近开展“黑飞”、偷拍、测绘等活动。境外间谍情报机关还可能结合其他渠道获取的信息进行多源数据交叉比对，拼凑成完整情报，甚至还可能对涉密单位工作人员以及周边居民、商户等人员开展针对性的渗透、拉拢和策反活动，对我国家安全构成严重威胁。 国家安全机关提示 《 中华人民共和国保守国家秘密法 》《 中华人民共和国测绘法 》《 公开地图内容表示规范 》等法律法规划出清晰底线：个人或者组织非法获取、持有、提供、利用属于国家秘密的地理信息的，将被依法追责。开放地图不是个人兴趣的“涂鸦板”，看似无心的标注可能触碰国家秘密“红线”。 ——绷紧“安全弦”。增强国家安全意识，不在地图平台标注任何涉及军事基地、涉密单位的地理信息。 ——把好“出口关”。不在社交平台发布涉密场所周边照片、视频，拍照前留意背景是否涉及敏感场所，不转发、不扩散任何标注有涉密地理信息的地图内容。 ——当好“守护者”。如发现在公开地图标注涉密地理信息等危害国家安全的可疑情况，请及时通过12339国家安全机关举报受理电话、网络举报受理平台（ www.12339.gov.cn ）、国家安全部微信公众号举报受理渠道或者直接向当地国家安全机关进行举报。 Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

B2B provides participants with an overview of business ownership and is open to service members (including National Guard and Reserve) and military spouses. What’s your transition mission? Begin your journey Introduction to Entrepreneurship: The foundational two-day, in-person course provides you with an introductory understanding of business ownership. Continue your journey Optional Follow-on Courses: “B2B: Revenue Readiness” is an online course delivered through a partnership with Mississippi State University. Receive sign-up information once you complete the in-person introductory course. Box plot vs. violin plot comparison # Note that although violin plots are closely related to Tukey's (1977) box plots, they add useful information such as the distribution of the sample data (density trace). By default, box plots show data points outside 1.5 * the inter-quartile range as outliers above or below the whiskers whereas violin plots show the whole range of the data. A good general reference on boxplots and their history can be found here: https://vita.had.co.nz/papers/boxplots.pdf Violin plots require matplotlib >= 1.4. Violin plots show the distribution of the data as a rotated kernel density estimate (KDE) along with summary statistics similar to a box plot. pages.text: Boxing: Jorge Linares remains in ICE detention and facing deportation - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Linares fought 56 times in his professional boxing career By Mandeep Sanghera BBC Sport journalist Published 18 November 2026 Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares remains in the custody of US immigration authorities in Texas and is facing deportation. The 41-year-old Venezuelan was detained on Sunday when US Border Force and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested him at El Paso International Airport. "On October 26, 2023, he entered the country with permission to stay for a temporary period, but in defiance of our nation's laws, he overstayed his welcome. He will remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings," said an ICE spokesperson. "To be clear, a pending application or work authorisation does not confer legal status in the United States." Linares is based in Miami and has fought more than 10 times in America. The immigration law firm Wilner & O'Reilly are representing Linares and they denied their client was in the US illegally. "Mr Linares is authorised to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities," said a Wilner & O'Reilly statement. "We are in communication with ICE and are working to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. Immigration matters follow established procedures, and those procedures take time. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Br-12 Watchable Wildlife | Montana View Map In Full Screen This 200-acre prairie marsh in north central Montana holds a narrow reservoir about one mile long. This reservoir acts as a prairie pothole with its tailwaters slowly drying during the summer and fall. This water cycle permits waterfowl to hatch and raise young in this relatively isolated, resource-rich area, then move fledglings to major waters like the Missouri River. BR-12 also provides habitat for migrating waterfowl, upland birds, and upland wildlife species, so it’s not uncommon to observe 20-30 species in one spring day. Canvasback and redhead ducks regularly nest in the tailwaters, pelicans and tundra swans stop by for a rest and snack on their journeys, and even black terns (a species of concern) and loons have been observed utilizing BR-12’s “waterfowl facilities.” The area around BR-12 is short-grass prairie habitat. Species you might see associated with this habitat include chestnut-collared and McCowan’s longspur, horned lark, northern harrier, ferruginous hawk, Swainson’s hawk, burrowing owl, pronghorn, coyote, red fox, ground squirrel, and badger. Copy markdown In this article About branches Branches let you develop features, fix bugs, or safely experiment with new ideas in a contained area of your repository. You always create a branch from an existing branch. Typically, you might create a new branch from the default branch of your repository. You can then work on this new branch in isolation from changes that other people are making to the repository. A branch you create to build a feature is commonly called a feature branch or topic branch. See Managing branches within your repository . You can also use a branch to publish a GitHub Pages site. See What is GitHub Pages? . You must have write access to a repository to create a branch, open a pull request, or delete and restore branches in a pull request. See Access permissions on GitHub . About the default branch When you create a repository with content on GitHub, GitHub creates the repository with a single branch. This first branch in the repository is the default branch. The default branch is the branch that GitHub displays when anyone visits your repository. The default branch is also the initial branch that Git checks out locally when someone clones the repository. Close BrandonSimons_Aloe's Diary Mapping the Southern African grid from OpenStreetMap, and where the gaps are Posted by BrandonSimons_Aloe on 17 November 2026 in English . I run Aloe Energy, a small not-for-profit initiative working on energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa. We published a free interactive map of the Southern African Power Pool grid, and OpenStreetMap is its backbone, so I wanted to share how it was built and where OSM could use help. What we did. We took every OSM power line of 66 kV and above across the 12 SAPP countries (country extracts from November 2026). Where OSM had no line but an older public map did, we filled the gap from TANESCO (2015) and World Bank (2017) grid maps, but only for lines recorded as existing, with a known voltage, and more than about 3 km from any OSM line. A “Source and age” view on the map colors each line by where it comes from, so you can see exactly what is OSM and what is gap-fill. Where OSM is thin. Coverage is weakest in Tanzania, DR Congo and Angola. Those are the places where the map still leans on maps that are close to ten years old, and where new mapping would change the picture most. Substations named in national plans are often missing too. The map: https://aloeenergy.org/research/sapp-grid . pages.text: Braves host annual 44 Classic at Truist Park 2026 Skip to Content Credit: Atlanta Braves ATLANTA -- It’s been a historic summer for the Braves and youth baseball. The organization celebrated the Atlanta RBI 18U team winning the Nike RBI Senior World Series for the first time since 1998 , while welcoming in other youth baseball players to Truist Park for the Native American Showcase . Last weekend capped off the festivities with their seventh annual 44 Classic , a tribute to Hank Aaron, showcasing diverse high school baseball talent across the Southeast region of the United States. Seventy-four student athletes played in two games at Truist Park in front of college coaches, professional scouts and a small but rowdy local crowd on Sunday. They were separated by grade classification: 30 freshmen and sophomores in the Junior Division, and 44 juniors and seniors in the Senior Division. More than 80 percent of them were from the metro-Atlanta area. “They call Atlanta the mecca of baseball,” said Marquis Grissom, an Atlanta native and member of the Braves 1995 World Series team. “Hank Aaron put Atlanta on the map, he was a guy who always thought about creating an opportunity for others. pages.text: Brazil's Best Kept Secret: The Pantanal | National Geographic The marshes of the Pantanal region are home to an impressive variety of life, from jaguars and alligators to the imperiled hyacinth macaw. Photograph by Markus Mauthe, laif/Redux TRAVEL Brazil's Best Kept Secret: The Pantanal The Amazon rain forest may get all the attention, but when it comes to wildlife, South America's biggest biodiversity star is the Pantanal. By Avery Stonich Published June 7, 2016 • 6 min read I get my first hint of the Pantanal 's impressive biodiversity as soon as I get off the plane in Corumbá , Brazil. White splotches cover the tarmac like some sort of Rorschach test on steroids. Bird droppings, I come to realize. The tropical heat drapes over me like a wool blanket; the thick air carries the raw scents of nature, a mix of earthy and sour. Part national park, part UNESCO World Heritage site , the Pantanal is the world’s largest tropical wetland, covering over 70,000 square miles—an area the size of Washington State—in the smack-dab center of South America. Brazil can lay claim to most of the region, but, as nature recognizes no political boundaries, the Pantanal spills into neighboring Paraguay and Bolivia. And though it's often overshadowed by the Amazon rain forest to the north, the Pantanal quietly boasts the highest concentration of wildlife on the continent . Life in the Pantanal follows the ebb and flow of an epic ecosystem that pulses with the seasons like a beating heart. pages.text: Brian Mann : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Brian Mann Enlarge this image Nancie Battaglia/NPR Nancie Battaglia/NPR Brian Mann Correspondent, National Desk Brian Mann is NPR's first national addiction correspondent. He also covers breaking news in the U.S. and around the world. Mann began covering drug policy and the opioid crisis as part of a partnership between NPR and North Country Public Radio in New York. After joining NPR full time in 2020, Mann was one of the first national journalists to track the deadly spread of the synthetic opioid fentanyl, reporting from California and Washington state to West Virginia. After losing his father and stepbrother to substance abuse, Mann's reporting breaks down the stigma surrounding addiction and creates a factual basis for the ongoing national discussion. Mann has also served on NPR teams covering the Beijing Winter Olympics and the war in Ukraine. During a career in public radio that began in the 1980s, Mann has won numerous regional and national Edward R. Murrow awards. He is author of a 2006 book about small town politics called Welcome to the Homeland , described by T he Atlantic as "one of the best books to date on the putative-red-blue divide." Mann grew up in Alaska and is now based in New York's Adirondack Mountains. His audio postcards, broadcast on NPR, describe his backcountry trips into wild places around the world. pages.text: Brian Trammell – Internet Society ‹ Back Biography Brian Trammell is a Staff Site Reliability Engineer at Google in Zürich, Switzerland, where he works on the management and measurement of datacenter reconfiguration and the production machine lifecycle. His interest in the Internet dates to 1993, when he first came online and decided he wanted to be part of making it better for everyone — a conviction that led him first to a sysadmin role at Georgia Tech, and then to network security measurement work at Carnegie Mellon's Software Engineering Institute, launching a career spanning Internet measurement, protocol engineering, and standards development. Brian has been active in the IETF since 2004 and served as a member of the Internet Architecture Board from 2014 to 2020. His standards and research work has centered on the transport layer and on the tension between protocol evolution, network manageability, and user privacy. He currently co-chairs the IETF's SCONE working group, which addresses transport-layer encryption and network observability, and the IRTF's Path Aware Networking Research Group. Prior roles in the Internet engineering ecosystem include chairing the IP Performance Measurement working group in the IETF and the RIPE Measurement, Analysis, and Tools working group. Before joining Google, he spent more than a decade as a researcher at ETH Zürich, focused on Internet performance measurement and the deployability and evolvability of Internet protocols. pages.title: Briefing: The Apache Way | Apache Software Foundation
pages.text: Briefing: The Apache Way | Apache Software Foundation Briefing: The Apache Way Ask The Apache Software Foundation’s Members about The Apache Way and you’ll get as many answers as to what it is. In fact, we surveyed the greater Apache user and developer community and were fascinated with their responses “The Apache Way to me…” What makes The Apache Way so hard to define? ¶ The Apache Way is a living, breathing interpretation of one’s experience with our community-led development process. Apache projects and their communities are unique, diverse, and focused on the activities needed at a particular stage of the project’s lifetime, including nurturing communities, developing great code, and building awareness. What is important is that they embrace: Earned Authority: all individuals are given the opportunity to participate, but their influence is based on publicly earned merit – what they contribute to the community. Merit lies with the individual, does not expire, is not influenced by employment status or employer, and is non-transferable (merit earned in one project cannot be applied to another). More on merit . Community of Peers: individuals participate at the ASF, not organizations. The ASF’s flat structure dictates that roles are equal irrespective of title, votes hold equal weight, and contributions are made on a volunteer basis (even if paid to work on Apache code). The Apache community is expected to treat each other with respect in adherence to our Code of Conduct . Domain expertise is appreciated; Benevolent Dictators For Life are disallowed. pages.text: Bringing Elastically Deterministic Data Loading to TorchTitan with Zephon - PyTorch Search Close Search Blog Bringing Elastically Deterministic Data Loading to TorchTitan with Zephon By Josh Wills, Maximilian Böther, Ties Robroek and the Zephon team October 16, 2026 No Comments Featured projects Why Zephon? The data that a model sees during training is one of the most powerful levers we have for influencing how well it performs. Much of the day-to-day work of improving a model happens on the data side: we change the mixture, or the filters that we apply, or how we tokenize and pack the samples, and then we run an ablation experiment to see whether the change helped. The first problem with this is that each of these changes often requires us to do a full pass over our training corpus and run expensive offline operations to prepare the data and store it on disk before our ablation experiment can run. Since a typical training run reads through that copy exactly once, and because most experiments don’t end up producing a better model, we spend a lot of time and storage creating datasets that will never be read again. This matters even more now that experiments can be designed, launched, and interpreted by agents instead of people. Agents are great for running lots of experiments in parallel, but they aren’t especially good at noticing when a result actually depends on something other than the change they made, like the number of GPUs that an experiment happened to run on (in fairness to the agents, humans aren’t great at noticing this either). pages.text: Bringing ExecuTorch to Arm Cortex-M CPUs - PyTorch Search Close Search Blog Bringing ExecuTorch to Arm Cortex-M CPUs By RJ Ascani (Meta), Adrian Lundell (Arm), Siddartha Pothapragada (Meta), Digant Desai (Meta), Zingo Andersen (Arm), Måns Nilsson (Arm), Erik Lundell (Arm) October 15, 2026 No Comments Featured projects TL;DR Deploying PyTorch models on microcontrollers has historically required converting to other framework formats, maintaining separate toolchains, and debugging cross-framework numerical mismatches. ExecuTorch eliminates this conversion step entirely. The Cortex-M backend enables PyTorch models to run directly on Arm Cortex-M CPUs with Arm CMSIS-NN acceleration. It supports all capability tiers (Scalar, DSP, and MVE/Helium) from a single workflow. We benchmark four of the five models from the MLPerf Tiny suite on the Alif Ensemble E8. Each model runs in 21.5 ms or less and uses under 90 KiB of RAM on a single Cortex-M55 core. For heterogeneous SoCs, the Cortex-M backend also provides the CPU execution path alongside Ethos-U NPU delegation. Minimal binary footprint. The ExecuTorch core runtime is under 20 KiB of flash, and operator selective build links only the operators your model needs, so total code size scales with the model rather than the framework. The official sign on the banks of the River Tone at French Weir Park in Taunton advises people not to swim. But that hasn't stopped Jo, Jenny, Sue and a second Jo from enjoying a regular dip together. "People think, oh you're swimming down by the supermarket, that can't be very nice, but it's gorgeous," Jenny Hillier says, as the women huddle round with their coats and hot drinks after a bracing October plunge. People have been swimming at the spot on the River Tone in the centre of Taunton for more than a hundred years. But it is only since 2024 that French Weir Park has been designated an official bathing site, which means from May to September the water gets tested by the Environment Agency (EA).
